newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt 1996 passenger traffic gains 1.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt 1996 passenger traffic gains 1.5 pct.

text.p: Passenger numbers at Frankfurt Airport rose 1.5 percent to a new record of 38.77 million in 1996, airport authority Flughafen Frankfurt Main AG (FAG) said.
But weak domestic demand from business travellers and moderate leisure travel demand kept growth last year at a lower level than in previous years, a FAG market research department report said.
Domestic passenger numbers at Frankfurt fell two percent to seven million while international traffic rose 2.5 percent to 31 million, the report said.
Leading growth destinations were the Far East, northern Africa and Central America, it noted.
The weak business travel demand last year was influenced by German economic decline, FAG said.
But leisure travel was boosted by stable or reduced holiday prices from tour operators, it added.
Frankfurt was also hit by an increase in direct international flights from other German airports, particularly to rival European hubs.
Competitor airlines also succeeded in winning traffic from Deutsche Lufthansa AG by adding new routes and under-cutting prices, the report said.
In December, passenger numbers at Frankfurt rose only 0.8 percent to 2.69 million due to flight cancellations caused by bad weather, FAG said.
"Without these cancellations, passenger figures would have been two percent higher than in the same month last year," the report said.
These hit mostly domestic traffic which fell 4.4 percent while intercontinental traffic grew four percent, it added.
